skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, video, LLMs, search, audio, 3D, and social automation.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh cloud AI apps from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: inference-shell

security_audit.summary: Confirmed issues are concentrated in installation guidance: the skill recommends curl piped directly to sh and uses dynamic shell command substitution for manual downloads. Many URL, environment variable, filesystem, and Markdown backtick alerts are documentation false positives, but the skill also enables account-impacting cloud app actions that require user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Remote install script is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl piped to sh with a pinned release download that verifies checksum and Sigstore signature before execution.

remediation.issue: Manual install command expands a remote manifest inside the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Use fixed release URLs or a trusted package manager, quote shell variables, and validate file names before downloading.

remediation.issue: Cloud app commands can perform account-impacting actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before posting, messaging, following, spending credits, or publishing generated content.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation commands increase supply-chain scope.
remediation.suggestion: Move optional skill installation to separate documentation and pin package or skill versions where possible.

semantic_findings.description: The skill demonstrates x/post-tweet and lists Twitter/X actions such as DM, follow, like, and retweet. A mistaken agent run could perform external account actions through the user's authenticated inference.sh account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly show posting to Twitter/X and list additional social actions. This is intended functionality, but it has clear account-impact risk.

semantic_findings.title: Secondary Skill Installation Commands

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are optional documentation, but they are concrete installation commands for additional skills. This creates a realistic supply-chain expansion path if followed.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need one interface for many hosted AI models. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Helps install and authenticate the inference.sh CLI.
Lists and searches available apps by category, keyword, featured status, or recency.
Retrieves app details and sample inputs before execution.
Runs cloud apps for image, video, text, audio, search, 3D, and social workflows.
Checks task status and saves outputs for long-running jobs.
Points users to specialized related skills for focused workflows.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, installed CLI, and valid credentials.
Runs hosted services, so costs, quotas, latency, and availability are external.
App schemas, model names, and provider behavior can change outside the skill.
Account-impacting actions need explicit confirmation before execution.

use_cases.title: Prototype Media Workflows
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, audio, and 3D assets from cloud models without managing local GPU infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Compare Hosted AI Apps
use_cases.description: Search app catalogs, inspect input requirements, and select a model before running production experiments.

use_cases.title: Automate Long Tasks
use_cases.description: Submit long-running cloud jobs, track task status, and retrieve output files after completion.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Find an inference.sh app for image generation. Show the best candidates and explain when to use each one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the selected app, generate a sample input, and tell me what fields I should edit before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Track a Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this selected inference.sh app with my approved input, then track the task until the result is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-App Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that searches for source material, generates media, and saves outputs. Ask before any paid or publishing step.

output_examples.input: Find a model for a product mockup image.
output: Recommended a flexible image generation app for mockup prompts.
Flagged cost and account requirements before running.

output_examples.input: Start a short video generation task and check progress.
output: Prepared the app input from the requested scene.
Reported status and where to retrieve the final video.

output_examples.input: Compare search apps for current web research.
output: Listed Tavily and Exa options with their expected strengths.
Suggested the best app for answer synthesis.
Recommended checking schema details before the first run.

best_practices: Inspect app schemas before running a new model.
Use saved input files for repeatable runs and easier review.
Confirm any action that spends credits, posts content, or changes an external account.
anti_patterns: Do not run account-impacting commands without explicit user approval.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts or shared files.
Do not assume app names, schemas, or output formats remain stable over time.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant use the inference.sh CLI to find, run, and track hosted AI apps.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require an inference.sh account and authenticated CLI session.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for image, video, audio, text, search, 3D, and social apps.

faq.question: Can it use Claude or OpenRouter models?
faq.answer: Yes. The listed app categories include Claude models through OpenRouter and other LLM providers.

faq.question: Is local GPU hardware required?
faq.answer: No. The examples run models through hosted inference.sh apps in the cloud.

faq.question: What should users confirm before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should confirm paid jobs, publishing actions, credential setup, and any command that affects external accounts.
